1| # beacond
2| 
3| beacond is a small self-hosted webhook relay. Producers publish events
4| to a single ingest endpoint; beacond persists them in a local queue and
5| fans each event out to every subscribed endpoint, retrying failures so
6| producers never have to.
7| 
8| ## How it works
9| 
10| - Publishes are authenticated by a shared-secret request MAC.
11| - Accepted events land in a durable queue before the HTTP response is
12|   sent, so an accepted publish survives a crash.
13| - Delivery workers claim events from the queue in small batches and
14|   post them to subscribers, with backoff on failure.
15| - Oversized payloads are rejected at the door.
16| 
17| ## Layout
18| 
19| - `cmd/beacond` — process entrypoint
20| - `internal/relay` — ingest handler and delivery fanout
21| - `internal/queue` — durable event queue
22| - `internal/sign` — request signing
23| - `internal/config` — configuration loading
